title: March Madness viewership soars to a 33-year high as marketers eye sports opportunities

facts.fact: The EMARKETER article 'March Madness viewership soars to a 33-year high as marketers eye sports opportunities' was published on 2 April 2026.
The EMARKETER article headline states that March Madness viewership reached a 33-year high; this is the publisher's headline claim and the chunk contains no supporting data.
facts.quote: March Madness viewership soars to a 33-year high as marketers eye sports opportunities

facts.fact: The article is credited to Marisa Jones and dated April 2, 2026.
A related EMARKETER article headline reports Oura's acquisition at $625 million.
facts.quote: Oura’s $625 million acquisition brings medical care into the wearable experience

facts.fact: March Madness TV viewership was the tournament's strongest in 33 years, up 9% year over year, averaging 10.3 million viewers across TBS, CBS, TNT, and TruTV, per Nielsen.
facts.quote: March Madness TV viewership was the tournament’s strongest in 33 years, up 9% YoY and averaging 10.3 million viewers across TBS, CBS, TNT, and TruTV, per Nielsen.

facts.fact: The Sunday Duke-UConn game was the peak viewing moment, averaging 13.4 million viewers, up 15% year over year, per the article.
facts.quote: Viewership peaked during Sunday’s Duke-UConn match, which drew in nearly 19 million viewers with an average of 13.4 million, up 15% YoY.

facts.fact: The Friday window featuring St. John's-Duke and Michigan-Alabama drew 14.2 million viewers, up 38% year over year, the most-watched in that slot since 1992.
facts.quote: The Friday window featuring St. John’s-Duke and Michigan-Alabama drew 14.2 million viewers, up 38% YoY and the most-watched in that slot since 1992.

facts.fact: Audiences for the first two rounds of March Madness broke records, averaging 10.1 million viewers.
facts.quote: Audiences for the first two rounds broke records, averaging 10.1 million viewers.

facts.fact: Nearly 50% of the US population are live sports viewers, according to EMARKETER's forecast.
facts.quote: Nearly 50% of the US population are live sports viewers, per our forecast.
